author_goal: Demonstrate that a relation-free hierarchical graph (Tri-Graph) with lightweight construction and a two-stage retrieval approach (entity activation via semantic bridging + global importance aggregation via PageRank) can outperform graph-based RAG methods while achieving linear scalability and zero LLM token cost during indexing. Develop a retrieval-augmented generation system that efficiently handles complex, multi-hop queries over large-scale unstructured corpora by eliminating reliance on error-prone relation extraction, using only entity-based graph indexing and a two-stage retrieval mechanism.

author_story_spine.title: Build Tri-Graph: extract entities from corpus passages, create entity, sentence, and passage nodes, and link them using
author_story_spine.author_statement: Build Tri-Graph: extract entities from corpus passages, create entity, sentence, and passage nodes, and link them using only occurrence relationships (contain and mention edges) – no relation triples. For each query, extract initial entities and compute a query–sentence similarity vector to capture contextual relevance. Iteratively propagate entity activation through the sentence–entity subgraph, aggregating similarity signals to activate intermediate bridging entities; apply dynamic threshold pruning to avoid explosion. Use the activated entities as seeds for personalized PageRank on the passage–entity subgraph, initializing passage nodes with a hybrid score (direct query–passage similarity + entity-based evidence). Retrieve the top‑k passages by final PageRank score.

author_intent_unverified_points.statement: Motivation: revisit GraphRAG shortcomings from relation extraction errors
LinearRAG overview: Tri‑Graph concept and two‑stage retrieval philosophy
Offline Tri‑Graph construction (entities, sentences, passages, contain/message adjacency matrices)
First retrieval stage: relevant entity activation via local semantic bridging (initialization, iterative propagation, dynamic pruning)
Second retrieval stage: passage retrieval via global importance aggregation (hybrid passage initialization, personalized PageRank)
Use a hierarchical graph that preserves original text (passages, sentences) alongside entities.
Decouple retrieval into a local entity‑activation stage and a global passage‑ranking stage.
Apply dynamic pruning with a fixed relevance threshold during propagation.
Employ personalized PageRank on the passage‑entity graph for passage retrieval.
Initialize passage PPR scores with a hybrid of direct similarity and entity‑based evidence.
spaCy NER: Lightweight named entity extraction used both offline (graph building) and online (query entity extraction).
author_intent_unverified_points.reason: Obligation has no typed behavior targets to align against facts.

author_intent_unverified_points.statement: Entity Activation via Semantic Bridging: Iterative propagation of entity relevance through the sentence–entity subgraph based on query–sentence similarity; identifies latent intermediate entities for multi‑hop connections.
author_intent_unverified_points.reason: Every typed target has a matching fact, but no authorized atomic claim is bound to this authoring obligation.

author_intent_unverified_points.statement: Dynamic Pruning: Threshold‑based filtering that retains only strongly relevant entities during propagation, preventing combinatorial expansion and noise.
author_intent_unverified_points.reason: Every typed target has a matching fact, but no authorized atomic claim is bound to this authoring obligation.

author_intent_unverified_points.statement: Personalized PageRank: Global importance aggregation on the passage–entity subgraph; ranks passages by propagating influence from activated entities.
author_intent_unverified_points.reason: Every typed target has a matching fact, but no authorized atomic claim is bound to this authoring obligation.

author_intent_unverified_points.statement: Hybrid Passage Initialization: Combines direct query–passage similarity with entity‑based statistics (occurrence, level) to set initial PPR scores for passage nodes.
author_intent_unverified_points.reason: Every typed target has a matching fact, but no authorized atomic claim is bound to this authoring obligation.
